text:
maya: FYI acme-inc reports their app getting NXDOMAIN for svc.acme.internal and when they manually hit the forwarder IP they get a cert for prod.redwood.com so TLS SNI mismatch.

alex: Can you paste minimal repro (dig/curl) from an app host?

maya: From their app host:
$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @10.0.2.2
;; -> NXDOMAIN

and: 
$ curl -v --connect-to svc.acme.internal:443:10.2.3.4 https://svc.acme.internal/
* Connected to 10.2.3.4 (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: Server certificate: CN=prod.redwood.com
* SSL: certificate subject name 'prod.redwood.com' does not match target 'svc.acme.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name mismatch

samir: Two simultaneous symptoms: tenant DNS returning NXDOMAIN then forwarder resolving to public/prod and presenting prod cert. Likely private hosted zone not associated to tenant VPC or resolver rule pointing to central forwarder without tenant override.

alex: @maya please collect Route53 private hosted zones + resolver rules & associations in tenant account and the central account. Also check VPC association for the zone owning svc.acme.internal.

maya: Tenant account checks:
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --query "HostedZones[?Name=='svc.acme.internal.']"
[]
$ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=DomainName,Values=acme.internal
[{ "Id": "rslvr-tenant-01", "DomainName": "acme.internal", "RuleType": "FORWARD", "ResolverEndpointId": "rslvr-end-111" }]
$ aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids vpc-0a1b2c
{ "EnableDnsSupport": true, "EnableDnsHostnames": true }

Tenant has a FORWARD rule for acme.internal to central forwarder 10.2.3.4, but no private hosted zone for svc.acme.internal in tenant account. The private zone appears owned by prod account and only associated with prod VPCs.

infra-bot: Flow logs show UDP/TCP queries from tenant VPC to 10.2.3.4 and the forwarder returning A records for prod endpoints; TLS logs show server presenting prod.redwood.com cert for that connection.

samir: Root cause hypothesis: missing private zone association for tenant VPC -> queries go to central forwarder -> forwarder resolves public/prod records -> TLS SNI mismatch.

alex: Remediation options: 
1) Associate the authoritative private hosted zone that contains svc.acme.internal with the tenant VPC (preferred when the zone should be shared).
2) Create a tenant-scoped private hosted zone with the needed A/ALIAS and associate it with the tenant VPC (if isolation per-tenant is desired).
3) Adjust resolver rules so a higher-priority rule forwards ONLY svc.acme.internal to a tenant-specific resolver.

Also confirm egress: since curl reached 10.2.3.4:443 we know egress is allowed; if timeouts were occurring we'd check security groups/NACLs and egress allowlists.

maya: Quick validation checklist I ran: 
- tenant has NO private hosted zone for svc.acme.internal 
- tenant resolver rule forwards acme.internal to central forwarder 
- forwarder returns prod answers and presents prod cert 

samir: Short-term workaround: create tenant private zone with the record and associate to tenant VPC. Long-term: agree on ownership (shared private zone vs tenant zones) and update resolver/forwarder logic to support per-tenant overrides.

alex: Runbook to associate existing zone (from zone owner account):
# from zone owner account
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z-ACME-01 --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c
If cross-account, run create-vpc-association-authorization in owner account first, then associate from tenant account or vice versa depending on trust model.

customer-sre: SRE asked if changing cert SAN to include svc.acme.internal is viable. It's doable but we'd rather not reuse prod certs in tenant scope. Fix DNS instead.

samir: Note: private hosted zone takes precedence over forwarding rules when associated with the VPC, so associating will resolve the NXDOMAIN.

alex: Also confirm forwarder isn't terminating TLS and injecting prod certs indiscriminately; infra-bot logs show it simply returned public IPs and TLS was with the public backend. No SNI rewriting.

customer-sre: We'll apply change today: either associate shared zone or create tenant zone. Will post assoc-id and dig after change. ETA EOD.

(1h later)

customer-sre: Applied change: associated hosted zone Z-ACME-01 with vpc-0a1b2c. Verification:
$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @10.0.2.2
10.10.12.34
$ curl -v https://svc.acme.internal/
* TLS handshake: certificate CN=svc.acme.internal
* <snip> 200 OK

maya: Marking resolved. Root cause: private hosted zone not associated with tenant VPC; central forwarder returned prod/public answers causing TLS SNI mismatch. Will re-open if customer reports regressions within 24h. :white_check_mark:
